title: Who built it, and where they went
lede: Ages and titles are those printed in the prospectus. We include later careers only when we found a source.

people.name: Louis Borders
people.text: Age 51 in the prospectus. Founded Borders Books in 1971 and Webvan in December 1996. Owned 28.3% before the IPO, the largest stake. He left the board in February 2001.[^1][^14]

people.name: George Shaheen
people.text: Age 55. Ran Andersen Consulting, later Accenture, for ten years before joining. Became chairman in February 2001 and resigned two months later, saying “a different kind of executive is needed.”[^1][^14][^18]

people.name: Robert Swan
people.text: Joined in October 1999 and was named CEO on April 26, 2001. He presided over the Atlanta closure and the July shutdown.[^15][^16]

people.name: Kevin Czinger
people.text: Age 40 in the prospectus, listed as a senior vice president who had earlier served as chief financial officer.[^1]

people.name: David Beirne
people.text: Benchmark held 12.3% before the IPO. Directors also included Tim Koogle of Yahoo and Christos Cotsakos of E*Trade.[^1]

people.name: Doug Herrington
people.text: Served on Webvan’s executive team before founding KeepMedia.[^22]
people.later: Joined Amazon in 2005, led the teams that launched Amazon Fresh, and became CEO of Worldwide Amazon Stores in 2022.[^22]

people.name: Mick Mountz
people.text: Saw at Webvan how inefficient pallet-and-case fulfillment was, and left in 2000.[^23]
people.later: Founded Kiva Systems, which Amazon bought for $775M in 2012 and turned into Amazon Robotics.[^19][^23]
